review: It was easy and quick to check in for the appointment I didn t have to wait too long The nurse was efficient Yes I came in for a routine smear test and wasn t expecting it to be painful However when the nurse inserted and pressed down on the speculum it was very painful indeed She didn t ask if it was painful Instead she just pushed down harder on the speculum and told me to relax which is impossible to do when you re in so much pain She should have stopped pushing down on the speculum and then told me to relax which would have been much easier to do while not in pain Instead I had to try to relax while in a lot of pain which was very difficult to do I think all nurses who administer smear tests should be aware of how much it can hurt if you re not totally relaxed They should not be in such a rush to finish the job and instead give all patients ample time to relax I ve never had a good smear test at this surgery During my last smear test I was given a speculum that was much to big and told to insert it myself without any lube or gel whatsoever Terribly painful The time before that I was asked if I minded having a student nurse administer the test I agreed but when they came in what I assumed to be a female student nurse was in fact a blushing young man which I hadn t been warned about He was unable to perform the test properly and had to be helped by the nurse and the whole test ended up being very painful as it was impossible to relax in such a situation I wouldn t have normally minded having a male nurse do the test but because he was clearly so embarrassed and red in the face plus unable to actually perform the test without help it made for a very embarrassing and tense situation I think all the nurses at Violet Melchett should be more careful and better trained around smear tests My own sister and several of my friends refuse point blank to even come in to your surgery anymore for smear tests They would rather risk cervical cancer than have to put up with the pain and embarrassment of a smear test when it s not handled right And I wish I could reassure them that it s painless like it s supposed to be but the fact is I ve never had a smear test at your surgery which hasn t been extremely painful One of my friends said she d rather go through childbirth again than come back to your surgery for a smear test So your nurses mishandling of a test that should be painless is putting several people I know and love in danger of developing cancer This is why I m writing such a detailed report and begging you to PLEASE retrain your nurses to give much better smear tests and give them a longer appointment time for this very important test which cannot be performed with any time pressure if you truly want the patient to be relaxed Total relaxation is the only way to perform this test painlessly and that requires time with also the option for the patient to insert the speculum herself but with lube Otherwise you are not offering a service which all women can use as the pain is too severe for many And I was sore down there for the next couple of days which is really inexcusable for a test that should be no more painful than regular intercourse

review: Dr PERSON called me back promptly listened with full attention and then decided I needed to be seen by a specialist She booked me in while I was on the phone so the handover was seamless and required no agency in my part The specialist examined me and swiftly organised a physio appointment for the following day and referral to Phsiotherapy Women s health Pelvic Triage for further care Yes I had been held up for over a hour at the hospital pharmacy queuing for over A hour to collect my RA medication I called ahead to the surgery reception out of courtesy explaining the situation and saying that I d do my best to get to my appointment on time but that there was a possibility I d be a little late The senior receptionist told me that there would be no way I d be seen if I wasn t on time and suggested we reschedule I wasn t able to attend at any of the suggested times so said I d keep my appointment and do my best to make it on time She reiterated that I d not be seen if I was at all late When I got there 5 minutes late the young receptionist who greeted me was helpful and not at all phased when I explained that I would have to go and park my car I was seen as soon as I had done that with no sign that there was any problem I felt the senior receptionist s attitude was unhelpful and unnecessary It made me feel quite upset Also it would be great to have been able to be seen more quickly at the hospital but the surgery presumably has no control over that Also the physio exercises are helping in the interim

review: Feedback on Appointment and Service Accessibility I did not receive a reminder for my appointment which made planning difficult The feedback and complaint form is not clearly visible on the website menu pages or contact page It is only accessible via the search function which is complicated and creates barriers for users As a result I was forced to bring letters of feedback and complaint in person causing difficulties with mobility and delays in response Information exchange is not accessible Text messages are sent from two different accounts HPVMGP and NHSNoReply and some information is sent via email Patch and NHS login use different emails with no option to unify them This makes it hard to find organise and keep medical records The lack of advance reminders for appointments creates further barriers and increases the risk of missing appointments The only option to book an appointment is by phone I was placed under a 7 Day Embargo F2F next to my letter request appointment without clear information about what this means whether it applies to me or to general practice or the reasoning behind it I previously informed the receptionist team that I needed an experienced GP due to the need for particular attention and correction of my medical history Despite this I was given an appointment with a trainee GP These issues have created unnecessary barriers and difficulties for me I would like that accessibility and communication be improved and that my need for an experienced GP is respected in future appointments reminders of the appointments clear explanation of appointment bookings process and timeline Information exchange improvement with two way option with accessible options email

review: I am writing to provide critical feedback regarding my consultation on Friday the 20th During that appointment I presented with active blisters on both my index finger and forearm I explicitly informed the GP of my clinical history with HSV 1 and raised concerns that this new painful presentation could be shingles or a related viral spread The GP confirmed the viral nature of the blisters during the examination but opted for a wait and see approach providing no medication This was a significant diagnostic and therapeutic omission for the following reasons The 72 Hour Window Viral infections of this nature require immediate antiviral intervention to prevent replication If I had waited until the following Monday for a new consultation my condition would have deteriorated significantly Nerve Involvement I clearly reported forearm pain which combined with the blisters pointed to herpetic involvement of the nerve later identified as Herpetic Whitlow Patient Led Intervention Due to the lack of a prescription I was forced to self initiate treatment using residual Aciclovir and private sourcing My immediate action in the first 72 hours is the only reason the infection was contained As a patient I expect a GP to act with more vigilance when a viral infection is confirmed especially when the patient presents with a known history and active neurological pain I hope this feedback leads to a review of how viral outbreaks are triaged at this surgery

review: Initially I was a little concerned when the PATCHS response I received suggested providing 4 days of manual cuff readings as the surgery indicated it did not want to rely on wearable data I completely understand the need for clinically reliable measurements and I appreciate that guidance is traditionally based on validated cuff readings However I wanted to note that the device I am using Hilo is not a typical consumer wearable It has been evaluated in multiple clinical studies and is calibrated against cuff based measurements effectively providing continuous ambulatory style monitoring rather than isolated spot readings In this instance I had already supplied over 200 readings taken across different times of day which the second GP was happy to use to inform the medication adjustment I thought it might be helpful to share this feedback as these types of clinically validated continuous monitoring devices may become increasingly relevant alongside traditional cuff measurements Not really the second call was very helpful after I explained things

review: I am writing to formally document my experience with Dr PERSON and Dr PERSON which I consider to represent a significant failure in the standard of care I was entitled to receive Since December 2025 I have been suffering from considerable and ongoing pain resulting from foraminal stenosis a condition further complicated by a documented history of spinal injury Over the course of several months I made repeated attempts to obtain appropriate medical attention including both in person consultations and telephone appointments with the above named practitioners During each of these interactions I specifically and clearly requested an MRI scan which represents a standard diagnostic measure for a condition of this nature Despite these repeated requests neither Dr PERSON nor Dr PERSON took the necessary steps to investigate my condition appropriately More concerningly my documented history of spinal injury was entirely disregarded despite its clear clinical relevance to my presenting symptoms A patient s medical history must inform clinical decision making at every stage and the failure to account for it in this case is in my view indefensible As a direct consequence of this inaction I was compelled to seek care elsewhere and to change my GP practice entirely causing further delays to my treatment and adding unnecessary burden during an already difficult period I intend to share this account across multiple channels as I believe the wider public has a right to be informed I would strongly urge the relevant medical and regulatory bodies to review whether the practitioners concerned are meeting the standards of continuous professional development and patient centred care that their profession demands You need just to be more human beings and listen to people s needs

I could have 5 Fenbid gel instead of 10 Fenbid gel to help with neck shoulder pain I have been waiting 29 weeks for nerve root injections despite the referral coming from a Consultant Professor of Neurosurgery Immediately agreed There was a discussion about how to make a formal complaint to NHS West and North London On 05 12 25 an outstanding fully qualified experienced GP took my clinical history examined me and requested an ultrasound at C W hospital A clinician who has never met me never taken my clinical history nor examined me cancelled the ultrasound because it did not conform to the guidelines NHS W NL took 9 weeks to inform the Good Practice What has been achieved Did my pain go away No The GP Patient relationship could have been seriously undermined I am most fortunate that I am a patient of the Good Practice In December I had 4 appointments in 12 days The GP responsible was absolutely determined to help me and I am pleased to say that I am making good progress However I am aware that my experience probably wouldn t be the experience of other patients at other practices A patient goes to their GP The GP refers them for an ultrasound The patient patiently waits for an appointment After 9 weeks the GP finds out that the referral has been cancelled The patient has to go back to their GP to start the process all over again The next time their GP says they are going to refer them to a clinic or for imaging does the patient believe the GP will be successful Trust the GP Probably not I wish to make a complaint to NHS W NL to make them aware that rejections like this are undermining the GP patient relationship and that the NWL guidelines need to be revised I am aware that NHS resources are limited very stretched and inappropriate unjustified referrals would clog up the system but GP s and their clinical judgement should not be undermined GP s are being given an ever increasing workload and should be supported The GP was most supportive of me making this complaint to NHS W NL No

professional standards Dear Madam I write in my capacity as a registered patient of Kensington Park Medical Centre to raise formal concerns regarding interactions with the practice This correspondence is submitted in accordance with the practice s feedback procedure and the NHS Constitution for England It is intended as constructive feedback directed solely at the specific issues outlined below and does not seek to impugn the wider body of clinical or administrative staff 1 Communication preferences and threats concerning email or written correspondence I have been advised or threatened against sending emails or maintaining written records of interactions Under the General Medical Council s Good Medical Practice 2024 Domain 2 Patients partnership and communication registered medical practitioners must treat patients with kindness courtesy and respect listen to patients and acknowledge their concerns and knowledge of their own health and communicate in a manner that supports shared decision making The NHS Constitution affirms the right of patients to receive information in a form they can understand and to be involved in decisions about their care While practices retain operational discretion over preferred channels an absolute prohibition or threat in response to a patient s request for written communication risks undermining the partnership principle and may engage the duty to make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010 where a patient s health condition substantially and long term adversely affects their ability to articulate matters verbally 2 Audio recording of consultations with patient consent Patients in the United Kingdom are generally entitled to make audio recordings of consultations in which they participate for purely personal use Such recordings fall outside the scope of the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 when made for domestic personal purposes Article 2 2 c UK GDPR Guidance from the British Medical Association and commentary in the medical literature confirm that clinicians should not refuse to proceed with a consultation solely because a patient wishes to record it for personal reference Open discussion and mutual transparency are encouraged as a matter of professional courtesy and trust Accurate contemporaneous records including those generated by patients support patient safety and may assist in the prevention of incomplete or inaccurate entries that could contribute to diagnostic errors The World Health Organization s Patient Safety Rights Charter 2024 emphasizes the rights to information access to medical records and patient engagement Principles articulated by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights regarding the right to the highest attainable standard of health further underscore the importance of transparent information exchange 3 Consideration of written health information provided by the patient Where a patient has formally documented and submitted relevant health information in writing because of difficulties in verbal articulation arising from illness the failure to acknowledge consider or respond to that information in a clinically appropriate manner may fall short of the standards in Good Medical Practice requiring doctors to take account of patients concerns and to work in partnership The NHS Constitution and NICE guidance on patient experience reinforce the expectation that information will be provided and received in accessible formats 4 Threats of removal from the practice list The General Medical Council s guidance Ending your professional relationship with a patient states that a relationship should only be ended in rare circumstances A patient must not be removed solely because they have made a complaint In adherence to legal mandates the contractual clauses of the National Health Service General Medical Services Contracts align with the aforementioned recommendations Threats of removal in response to a patient s request for written communication or the exercise of the right to record for personal use would if substantiated raise serious questions under the above framework and under the Human Rights Act 1998 Articles 2 8 and 14 read with the Equality Act 2010 where disability is engaged 5 Professional standards and accountability I note that I hold professional qualifications myself Adverse treatment is not justified solely by a patient s polite and professional disagreement or their expression of a reasoned clinical opinion particularly when the patient is a qualified professional Any such response would risk inconsistency with the GMC s requirements of fairness respect and the avoidance of discrimination I acknowledge with appreciation the service provided by those members of the clinical and administrative team who continue to discharge their duties in accordance with professional standards and who are not implicated in the matters raised Requested resolution It is my polite request that the practice incorporate the following We kindly ask for a formal articulation on your website concerning the established protocol for written or email communications initiated by patients as well as the permission for private audio recording of consultations Review the specific interactions giving rise to these concerns and provide a substantive written or email response please Ensure that any future communications with qualified professional patients respect the legal and professional frameworks cited above please Should a satisfactory local resolution not be achieved I reserve the right to escalate the matter through the formal NHS complaints route to the relevant Integrated Care Board and if necessary the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman the Care Quality Commission or the General Medical Council as appropriate I also note the public interest considerations inherent in the transparent operation of publicly funded primary care services I trust that this feedback will be received in the spirit of continuous improvement that the practice s own patient advertisement encourages

review: I had a blood test on 27th Aug to test my PSA I was not told it would also test my testosterone levels so I carried on with Testogel meaning my levels would be normal On Saturday 29th Aug I get an alarming phone call from NHS 111 asking if I had diarrhoea dizziness palpitations etc because my potassium levels were very high I was advised to go straight to the nearest A E for a checkup I told the caller I had never felt better and ignored the crazy advice I had made a follow up call with the GP to discuss the results of my PSA test on Wednesday 9th 9am 12pm but when I called on Monday Monday 31st Aug to book another blood test I was told the 9th Sept phone call appointment was not registered I made another blood test appointment for Thursday 3rd Sept at 17 50 but that was cancelled on the day I now have another blood test on Thursday 10th at 11 30am tbh I don t know who is doing what and for what purpose Nobody is caring for me the person as opposed to me the number The nurse doesn t know what the Dr wants and the Dr asks for a test without checking with me first I appreciate appointments sometime are cancelled but I thought I had an appointment on 9th Sept and it was chance that told me otherwise Nothing is joined up and nothing reassures Yes one Dr giving clear instructions to the nurse having talked about it with me If I book an appointment with reception then put it in the system If you need to check the PSA then don t also check for testosterone when you know I m on Testogel
